quotes.text: The bottleneck persists not because of unwilling workers, but because of withheld tools. This is not a people problem. It's a tooling and governance problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the automation backlog as a tooling and governance issue.

quotes.text: The real breakthrough isn't about squeezing developers harder. It's about harnessing the rest of the crew.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the shift from developer-only automation to citizen development.

quotes.text: It's important to stress what citizen developers don't do. They don't displace it, they don't override security, and they don't hijack strategy. Their role is to extend it's reach.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies the role of citizen developers relative to IT.

quotes.text: The path forward is clear. Distribute automation, put guardrails in place, and empower citizen developers so your specialists can focus on strategy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise action plan for scaling Power Platform.

takeaways: Developer-only automation creates backlogs and burns out engineers on micro-tasks, while the people who know the work best are locked out.
Citizen developers using low-code Power Platform tools inside guardrails such as a Center of Excellence, admin controls and data loss policies extend IT's reach without losing control.
Forrester's Total Economic Impact research on Power Platform points to strong ROI and fast payback, and Power Automate lets you track the hours each flow saves.
hook: IT backlogs grow because every automation request funnels through a few developers. This episode helps IT and business leaders see how governed citizen development on Microsoft Power Platform clears the queue, frees developers for architecture and delivers measurable ROI.
